mcqs.q: During the examination, owners' negative behaviours had what effect on their dogs' anxiety signs?
mcqs.e: When owners attended, their negative behaviours intensified signs of anxiety in their dogs.

mcqs.q: Owners' visual and verbal attempts to comfort their dogs produced:
mcqs.e: Attempts to comfort had no significant effect on the dogs' stress.

mcqs.q: Increased canine stress-related behaviour was associated with:
o: Less eye contact with the owner
More eye contact with the owner
mcqs.e: More stress meant more eye contact, consistent with social referencing/reassurance-seeking.

mcqs.q: Improvement in global stress scores was observed in:
mcqs.e: All global scores improved (p<0.001) across all groups, including puppies.

mcqs.q: Compared with one-month reference pheromone products, the longer-lasting Zenidog devices were:
mcqs.e: Zenidog devices were as effective as the reference products but lasted longer.

mcqs.q: The main practical advantage of the Zenidog devices was:
mcqs.e: They matched reference efficacy while lasting two to three months instead of one.

mcqs.q: Could video stimuli alone localize all face/object processing regions of interest?
o: Yes, videos localized all the ROIs
mcqs.e: Using video conditions alone, all ROIs were localized in both dogs and humans.

mcqs.q: Which dog region responded significantly more to live faces than to video faces?
o: The area along the ectosylvian fissure
mcqs.e: Only the ectosylvian fissure area showed greater activation to live than video faces.

mcqs.q: Overall, live stimuli were suggested to be:
mcqs.e: Videos sufficed for localization, but live conditions may be more salient.

mcqs.q: Over the course of the mock veterinary visit, salivary cortisol, IgA, and infrared temperature:
mcqs.e: All three rose significantly from baseline through post-kennel and post-examination.

mcqs.q: The effect of music treatment on salivary cortisol was:
mcqs.e: Cortisol, IgA, and temperature increased regardless of music treatment.

mcqs.q: Dogs were scored as most 'afraid' during which phase?
mcqs.e: Dogs were more afraid during the physical examination than in the kennel.

mcqs.q: Environmental enrichment activities resulted in:
o: Increased relaxation and reduced stress behaviours
mcqs.e: EE significantly increased relaxation and reduced alert and stress behaviours.

mcqs.q: Which activities produced the greatest overall positive behaviour change?
o: Interactive toy and stuffed food toy
mcqs.e: Conspecific play and playhouse activities had the greatest positive change.

mcqs.q: The food-based enrichment activities showed:
mcqs.e: Interactive toy and stuffed food toy produced the least behaviour change.

mcqs.q: Overall SRB prevalence in the population between February and October 2020:
mcqs.e: Prevalence fell from 22.1% to 17.2% as time left alone also decreased.

mcqs.q: Which dogs were at greatest risk of developing new signs of SRB?
o: Those left alone more during lockdown
Those whose alone-time decreased most during lockdown
mcqs.e: Dogs whose leaving hours dropped most were at increased risk of new SRB.

mcqs.q: The findings link SRB risk primarily to:
o: Changes in owner routine/time left alone
mcqs.e: The study showed a link between changes in owner routine and SRB risk.

mcqs.q: The replication study concluded the Dog ARS is:
o: A reliable tool for ADHD-like behaviour
mcqs.e: Factor structure replicated with good internal consistency and test-retest reliability.

mcqs.q: In its current form, the Dog ARS is:
o: Not suitable to detect diagnosable individuals
mcqs.e: It cannot identify diagnosable individuals as currently constructed.

mcqs.q: A key limitation preventing diagnostic use was the absence of items assessing:
mcqs.e: The questionnaire lacks items on functional impairment needed for diagnosis.

mcqs.q: Did the study find clear evidence for jealousy-like behaviours in dogs?
mcqs.e: No clear evidence of jealousy-like behaviour was found in the triadic interactions.

mcqs.q: The dogs' behaviour was best explained by:
mcqs.e: Indicators pointed to behavioural synchronization with the caregiver.

mcqs.q: Dogs showed more friendly behaviour toward the fake dog when it was approached by:
mcqs.e: More dogs were friendly toward the fake dog when the caregiver interacted with it.

mcqs.q: The top reason owners gave for not seeking veterinary care was:
o: Lack of access to a veterinarian
mcqs.e: Lack of access to a vet (30%) was the leading reason for not seeking care.

mcqs.q: A dog's chronic illness diagnosis had what effect on the odds of seeking care during the pandemic?
mcqs.e: Chronic diagnosis reduced care-seeking due to difficulty accessing non-urgent care.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that separating owners from their dogs during consultations should be:
mcqs.e: Owner-dog separation should be avoided due to impacts on dogs, owners, and care-seeking.

mcqs.q: Dogs with high aggressive reactivity showed impairments in:
mcqs.e: High aggressive reactivity was associated with poorer self-control, not cognitive inhibition.

mcqs.q: Was cognitive inhibition associated with aggression?
mcqs.e: No association between cognitive inhibition and aggression was found.

mcqs.q: Compared with privately owned dogs, police dogs showed:
mcqs.e: Police dogs had higher aggression levels and poorer self-control.

mcqs.q: For what proportion of characteristics deemed important for adoptability was scientific support lacking?
mcqs.e: Evidence was lacking for over 85% of the characteristics organisations valued.

mcqs.q: How many of the screening factors were actually supported by scientific evidence?
mcqs.e: Only 10 factors were supported by the literature.

mcqs.q: Given the weak evidence base, the authors suggested organisations focus on:
o: Pre-adoption adopter education and post-adoption support
mcqs.e: They recommended emphasizing adopter education and post-adoption support.

mcqs.q: In this pilot, environmental enrichment and petting were found to be:
o: Both efficient and feasible for improving welfare
mcqs.e: Both methods proved efficient and feasible in the clinic setting.

mcqs.q: Compared with petting, environmental enrichment led dogs to:
mcqs.e: EE increased activity, with dogs walking and digging more.

mcqs.q: Dogs exhibited more positive social interactions after which intervention?
mcqs.e: Petting (direct human contact) produced more positive social interactions.
